summary: Establishes the authoritative student knowledge foundation through institution-wide discovery and roadmap design, with detailed Year One audit, governance proving and live implementation beginning in SASD through King’s Answers before progressive expansion across King’s.
detailSummary:
4.1.1 is the institutional knowledge work beneath the Digital Student Experience Hub rather than a CRM-delivery workstream. CRM, ticketing, case-management and enquiry workflow are inherited from the separately delivered King’s Answers and wider enquiry-management capability. This deliverable owns the quality, authority and operating model of the student-facing knowledge that those services consume.

The discovery boundary is institution-wide from the outset. King’s should identify the student-facing knowledge domains held across all relevant services and directorates, understand their current channels and ownership, and produce an exhaustive domain map and sequenced roadmap to eventual institutional coverage. This is a breadth exercise: it prevents the initial implementation boundary from becoming the long-term boundary without requiring a detailed audit and remediation of every service in Year One.

Detailed Year One implementation should begin with priority knowledge domains within SASD. This creates a bounded environment in which to test the information model, content standards, governance, ownership and operating model while using King’s Answers as the immediate self-service and enquiry-management proving environment. Existing SASD content will be audited and classified so priority material can be improved, consolidated, retired or newly authored rather than copied wholesale.

King’s Answers provides the first live feedback loop. Search behaviour, unresolved questions and enquiry demand should be used to test whether content is findable, sufficient, trustworthy and correctly owned. The same foundation is then made available for reuse through the Digital Student Experience Hub, with the proven SASD model progressively extended across the institution-wide roadmap according to student need, service readiness and evidence from the first implementation.

Senior knowledge/content architecture and governance leadership, plus authoritative subject ownership, are assumed to be protected existing institutional capacity. The business-case envelope includes a minimum 0.5 FTE of funded communications, content-design and editorial delivery capacity throughout mobilisation, profiled at £33,000 in each academic year using a £66,000 fully-loaded full-time benchmark, or £99,000 across three years. Organisationally this should be designed alongside the existing 2.4.4 activation and reputation capacity as a broader King’s Edge / Student Experience communications and content role or small capability. Accounting remains split: the existing King’s Edge allocation stays within 2.4.4 and this additional 0.5 FTE is charged to the Digital Student Experience Hub. Discovery and the first SASD implementation should be used to test whether wider institutional rollout requires additional capacity; 0.5 FTE is a minimum planning provision, not an assumption that one half-time post can remediate the full institutional knowledge estate.

steps.title: Discover the institutional student knowledge landscape and define the operating model
steps.summary: From September to November 2026, establish the institution-wide discovery baseline: identify student-facing knowledge domains across relevant services and directorates, current channels and ownership, and the main overlaps, gaps and dependencies. In parallel, define the boundary of authoritative student knowledge, including audience separation, content inclusion and exclusion rules, the distinction between durable information and opportunity content, taxonomy and metadata principles, authoritative ownership, editorial control, review and expiry expectations, and the relationship with King’s Answers, the Hub, web/DXP channels and staff-facing guidance. Produce an exhaustive domain map and sequenced roadmap to institutional coverage, while confirming SASD as the first detailed implementation boundary.

existingCapacity.role: Senior knowledge, content architecture and governance leadership
existingCapacity.owner: SASD, Communications/web and Digital Student Experience Hub governance; named lead to confirm
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide senior content and knowledge-design direction, establish the institutional model and standards, convene cross-institution decisions and connect the work to existing web, communications and service governance.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The work may produce content but fail to establish the institutional authority, standards and operating model needed for reliable cross-channel reuse.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide protected participation to identify authoritative policy and service knowledge, validate accuracy, resolve conflicts and accept ongoing ownership of governed domains.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: A central content function would be forced to infer policy or service truth and could not create a trustworthy knowledge foundation.

newInvestment.item: Hub share of shared communications and content delivery capacity
newInvestment.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub / King’s Edge programme leadership; institutional employment home to confirm
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Digital Student Experience Hub mobilisation investment
newInvestment.rationale: Provides hands-on content design, plain-English and accessibility editing, knowledge remediation, migration support and wider student-facing communications delivery. It is intended to form part of one broader communications and content capability alongside the existing 2.4.4 King’s Edge activation/reputation allocation, while remaining separately accounted for in the Hub business case.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Discovery may define a good knowledge model but SASD remediation, migration and wider adoption would depend on already stretched teams absorbing substantial editorial production work.

steps.title: Audit and classify priority SASD student knowledge
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, conduct the first detailed content audit within priority SASD knowledge domains. Identify authoritative sources and owners, classify content as retain, improve, consolidate, retire or redirect, identify gaps, and produce a sequenced SASD migration and rationalisation backlog. Use existing migration work and student-enquiry research as starting evidence rather than repeating discovery unnecessarily. The purpose is to prove the method in depth before extending detailed audit activity across the wider institutional roadmap.

existingCapacity.contribution: Support mapping of ownership, dependencies, content flows and service boundaries where needed during the first SASD audit.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The audit may identify content problems without sufficiently resolving process, ownership and dependency issues behind them.

existingCapacity.contribution: Validate authoritative sources, identify obsolete or conflicting material and agree the status and ownership of priority knowledge.

steps.title: Prepare and publish the first governed SASD knowledge domains through King’s Answers
steps.summary: From December 2026 to April 2027, improve, consolidate and author the first priority SASD knowledge domains using the agreed model, establish named content ownership and review dates, and make them available through King’s Answers. Do not migrate weak or unsuitable content simply to achieve coverage. Capture the effort, governance and editorial patterns required so later institutional rollout can be planned from evidence rather than assumption.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide the proving environment and technical publication route while CRM, ticketing and workflow remain outside 4.1.1 scope.
Approve substantive accuracy, ownership, review dates and any retirement or consolidation of competing material.

steps.title: Establish knowledge operations and the enquiry-evidence improvement loop
steps.summary: From February to June 2027, make authoring, approval, review, expiry, defect handling and ownership transfer operational for the first SASD knowledge domains. Define how search data, failed self-service, unresolved questions and enquiry demand identify missing or weak knowledge and feed a transparent improvement backlog. Use the live operating evidence to refine the model for wider institutional adoption.

steps.title: Make governed knowledge reusable through the Digital Student Experience Hub
steps.summary: From April to September 2027, establish the simplest safe and supportable way for the Hub to retrieve or surface governed SASD student knowledge for the focused first release, while preserving King’s Answers and enquiry management as separately delivered service capabilities. Use live student testing to confirm findability, sufficiency and hand-off where information alone is not enough.

steps.title: Extend the governed knowledge model across the institutional roadmap
steps.summary: From the first Hub release through the remainder of mobilisation, use the institution-wide domain roadmap and evidence from the SASD implementation to sequence detailed discovery, migration and governance adoption across all relevant student-facing services and directorates. Expand the governed model to additional priority domains, consolidate or retire redundant copies where continuity is proven, and use evidence from Hub use, King’s Answers and service demand to adjust sequencing. The roadmap should remain exhaustive in intended institutional coverage even where implementation is deliberately phased. Settle the enduring institutional knowledge ownership and operating capacity before mobilisation closes.

enablingConditions.condition: Use evidence from the SASD implementation to review whether the 0.5 FTE funded communications/content provision is sufficient for the pace and breadth of wider institutional rollout.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital Student Experience Hub governance with SASD and Communications/web
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before committing the first major post-SASD rollout wave
enablingConditions.whatItUnlocks: An evidence-based decision to retain, reshape or increase delivery capacity without treating the initial 0.5 FTE provision as a fixed ceiling.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The institutional roadmap may be sequenced faster than the available editorial and migration capacity can deliver safely.
